In this VladTV interview, Florida criminal defense attorney Bradford Cohen—known for representing Lil Wayne, Kodak Black, Drake, Rod Wave and Travis Scott—discusses his brief conversation with Lil Durk just one day before Durk’s arrest. Cohen explains why he found the timing and “fleeing” argument unusual, noting that authorities typically execute coordinated arrests at the same time to avoid warning co-defendants.

Cohen also breaks down the current state of the case, including witness credibility, Vonnie’s testimony, damaging jail calls, text message interpretations, and why he believes Durk was right not to take the stand. He compares the legal strategy to other high-profile trials, including the Diddy case, Mann Act charges and RICO arguments, while emphasizing that the jury’s decision may hinge on how they view cooperating witnesses.

Chingy joins VladTV to react to Sidney Starr’s arrest in Georgia following an alleged incident involving a 13-year-old boy at an Embassy Suites. Vlad breaks down reports that Starr’s bond was denied in Fulton County after a judge cited flight-risk concerns, with charges said to carry a potential 25-to-life sentence if convicted. The conversation also revisits Chingy’s prior encounter with Starr, public reactions to Starr’s appearance in jail, and Vlad’s broader discussion about sexuality, identity, disclosure, and late hip-hop figure Mister Cee. recentItems.title: Will Lil Durk Be Found Guilty Or Not Guilty??👀
DJ Vlad & Elliott Wilson Interview Hit Boy (Full Interview)
recentItems.description:
Watch the FULL uncensored interview early - become a VladTV YouTube Member now:
https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Grammy-winning producer Hit-Boy sits down with Vlad and Elliott Wilson for an in-depth conversation about success, music industry politics, financial independence, and the lessons he's learned producing for some of hip-hop's biggest artists.

Hit-Boy discusses the meaning behind his project Success Is a Dirty Word, explaining how achieving success can complicate relationships with friends and family. He opens up about investing significant money into his father's music career while dealing with the emotional and financial strain that came with trying to help someone close to him.

The conversation explores Hit-Boy's creative evolution and his legendary run with Nas, which produced six albums and roughly 80 songs in just three years. He reflects on being permanently associated with massive records like "N****s in Paris" while explaining why his catalog extends far beyond the hits he's best known for, including R&B and other styles of production.

Hit-Boy also gets candid about the business side of the music industry, detailing a restrictive production and publishing situation that limited his financial freedom despite producing diamond-level records. He discusses the difficulty of developing new artists compared to working with established stars like Kanye West and Jay-Z, as well as how streaming transformed the economics of the industry.

Later, Vlad and Hit-Boy discuss building wealth outside of entertainment. Vlad explains his long-term investments in companies like Amazon, Google, and Tesla, while Hit-Boy reveals his interest in expanding into film and television scoring, where he believes the business can be cleaner than traditional music royalties.

The conversation concludes with a discussion about wealth managers, investing, ownership, and why making money is only one part of achieving lasting financial independence.

Part 1: https://youtu.be/lOCPGaKuQxw
--------
In this VladTV segment, DJ Vlad asks Judge Greg Mathis about reports that singer d4vd has dropped high-priced defense attorneys and may rely on a public defender as a criminal trial looms. Vlad says he heard d4vd still has money in a trust controlled by his parents, joking that they may not want to spend more if the case is headed toward a guilty plea. Mathis laughs, then argues defendants should get every chance to hire the best lawyers, noting that top trial attorneys can “trip witnesses up” during cross-examination.

The conversation expands into Mathis’ time presiding over murder trials, which he describes as some of the hardest cases of his career. He reflects on guilty verdicts, victims’ families, young defendants failed by society, drugs, guns, and the justice system’s impact on Black youth.

Attorney Moe Gangat returns to VladTV with an inside look at major hip-hop legal battles, from Lil Durk’s federal murder-for-hire trial in Los Angeles to Duane “Keefe D” Davis being convicted in the Tupac Shakur murder case after just 90 minutes of jury deliberation in Nevada. Gangat breaks down why Keefe D’s own interviews and statements became powerful evidence, while Vlad compares the verdict with Judge Mathis’ view on reasonable doubt.

The conversation also covers dramatic testimony involving OTF, Vonnie Kayvon Grant, King Von, Quando Rondo, Lil Pab, Chicago, Miami, Georgia, and the Beverly Center shooting. Gangat weighs in on cooperating witnesses, rap lyrics in court, and whether defendants facing life should take the stand. Plus: updates and analysis on Tory Lanez and Megan Thee Stallion, Pooh Shiesty and Gucci Mane, Young Dolph’s case, Hernandez Govan, public defenders, trial coverage, and the rise of social media courtroom reporting.
